landmarks.what: globalThis Symbol.for('price-check.notifier') hand-off of main's DesktopNotifier to the server bundle; undefined outside Electron
seeds the desktop alert channel row once (never overriding user flags) and alerts now carry watchId plus an 'unsupported' failure reason
shows the app window on a same-origin path, falling back to the origin for off-app paths and never reloading a live window without one

findings.text: package.json version bump 0.1.3 -> 0.1.4 is not among the task's declared files (.gitleaks.toml, notify-bridge.ts, notify-bridge.spec.ts); confirm it belongs in this commit
notify-bridge.spec's no-import check also covers dynamic import(), require() and re-exports with 'from', which goes beyond the test_contract

ensureChannel works for any ChannelKind: if it were ever called for ntfy/resend/smtp, an unreadable row would be overwritten with an empty {} config. That is harmless for desktop, the only intended caller, and the old config could not be opened anyway.
The re-seal update only matches the blob it just read (configEnc equal to it, or null), so a config saved in between is left alone. The concurrent test covers the double-insert case.

src/desktop/window.ts:150 appUrl's catch returns origin on an unparseable path with nothing logged; the fallback is spec-mandated (fails isAppUrl) and the JSDoc states the off-app fallback, but the parse-failure case itself is not named and a dropped click target leaves no trace
the minimised-window test asserts restore() precedes show(), but not that restore() precedes the loadURL of the target, which the description's order (restore, load, then show/focus) implies
off-origin table goes beyond the contract (adjacent port, javascript:, unparseable 'http://[') and checks both the new-window and live-window paths
